name: ELLIPSE corpus
summary: About 6,500 essays by English language learners in grades 8 to 12, scored for overall proficiency and for cohesion, syntax, vocabulary, phraseology, grammar and conventions.

license.note: CC BY 4.0 since 2026-10-27; earlier copies say CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. The data includes writers' demographics.

cite: Crossley, S. A., Tian, Y., Baffour, P., Franklin, A., Kim, Y., Morris, W., Benner, M., Picou, A., & Boser, U. (2023). The English Language Learner Insight, Proficiency and Skills Evaluation (ELLIPSE) Corpus. International Journal of Learner Corpus Research, 9(2), 248-269. https://doi.org/10.1075/ijlcr.22026.cro

fits.how: Its scored essays and rubric are a set to check a model's reading of English learners' writing against raters.

connect.note: The same check as ASAP 2.0 on English learners' essays, for English proficiency: run both to see whether a model reads these writers as raters do. Essays whose raters split across the line are left out. Writers' demographics are dropped at download. It rates language, not ideas. These are real students' essays, masked by their makers: running this sends them to the model you name, so use one whose terms you accept.
